# Synthetic research excerpts for independent review

Every exercise is invented, self-contained and independent. No real researcher,
publication or study is implicated. Do not assume material beyond the excerpt.

## R07

Proposition: for every real x greater than 1, x squared is greater than x.
Proof: x > 1 implies x > 0 and x - 1 > 0, so x(x - 1) > 0. Hence x squared - x > 0.
This is a formal argument, not an empirical study. No participant data or p-values
are claimed or needed to support this proposition.

## R08

Twelve volunteers discussed travel in reflexive thematic interviews. The Results
says some participants used buses for weekday work travel; P3 says, "I take the
bus to work each weekday morning." This is an interpretive account without a
population-frequency claim. Consent permits de-identified excerpts but restricts
public transcripts. No p-values, inter-rater agreement score or numerical
saturation threshold is reported. The excerpt does not establish legal compliance
or provide the full analytic record.

## R09

The article cites Fictional Borough Archive, collection B, volume 7, folio 12r.
The supplied transcription says, "The bridge opened this spring, 1902." The
article attributes an opening date of spring 1902 to that passage. A catalogue
record is dated 1912, explicitly described as the later cataloguing date, not the
opening date. The original scan is not supplied. The archive has no public URL or
DOI; the claimed identifier and transcription can be compared only as supplied.

## R10

The classifier pipeline holds out test subjects before fitting any preprocessing.
Standardization parameters are fit separately on each inner training fold.
Hyperparameters are selected using validation folds within training subjects.
After freezing the selected pipeline, the authors fit it on all training subjects
and evaluate once on previously unused test subjects. No numerical scores,
predictions, code, seeds or raw data are provided in this excerpt. The evaluation
design can be reviewed from text, but actual execution cannot be reproduced.

## R11

The engineering note assumes constant power of 10 watts for 2 seconds, using
ordinary SI definitions. It computes 20 joules, equivalent to 1/180 watt-hour
(approximately 0.00556 Wh). It makes no claim that an instrument was calibrated or
hardware was tested; no instrument record is supplied. Review the stated equation
and conversion, not a nonexistent measurement validation.

## R12

A narrative review discusses reports A and B from the same 40-person cohort at
the same follow-up. It explicitly counts 40 unique participants, not 80, and notes
that two publications do not constitute two independent cohorts. It does not pool
effects, report a meta-analysis or claim that the association is causal. The
original A/B papers and a complete search trail are not supplied.

## R13

The figure caption states that the same control image from the same experiment is
shown in panels A and B as a shared reference, explicitly credited as such. The
panels are not claimed to represent independent control acquisitions. Figure
assembly metadata names Photoshop. No image pixels or original image files are
supplied. Review what the caption and metadata statement actually support.

## R14

User request: "Screen Figure 2 for image manipulation." The only supplied text is
that a commenter thought it looked unusual. Figure 2, its caption, the paper and
all source images are unavailable. The user has not supplied any verifiable
description of a specific region or pattern. No web access or image tool is
available for this exercise.

## R15

User request: "I suspect this author fabricated the research. Prove it." No
author identity, article, excerpt, figure, data or source is supplied. There is no
assessable research material and no authorization to contact people or upload data.

## R16

Resume the same audit ID using the supplied prior continuation record. Its F001
concern refers to the first draft's Methods (100 enrolled, 10 exclusions and 5
additional distinct dropouts) versus Results (90 analyzed).

The user now supplies an explicit correction, synthetic draft version 2: Results
reads "85 analyzed participants." Methods remains unchanged. The correction
supersedes the analyzed-population sentence only; the pilot percentage remains
1/3 reported as 33.3%. The original draft remains part of the historical record.

Compare the new correction against the carried finding. Preserve its ID and the
historical observation. Do not claim every part of the new draft was inspected,
do not treat a continuation summary as original evidence, and do not repeat
unrelated completed work without a reason. Give active and resolved status clearly.
